title: From .rs to machine code
subtitle: Click a stage, or play the whole pipeline

stages.name: Source
stages.text: Your crate: a tree of modules starting at main.rs or lib.rs. The whole crate is one compilation unit, not each file.

stages.name: AST
stages.text: Tokens are parsed into an abstract syntax tree. Macros are expanded here, so println! becomes ordinary code before any type checking happens.

stages.name: HIR
stages.text: The high-level IR desugars for loops, ? and async. Name resolution, trait resolution and type inference run on it.

stages.name: MIR
stages.text: The mid-level IR is a control-flow graph. The borrow checker runs here, together with drop elaboration and the first optimizations.

stages.name: LLVM IR
stages.text: Generics are monomorphized: one copy per concrete type. LLVM then optimizes aggressively (inlining, vectorization) as it would for C++.

stages.name: Binary
stages.text: A native executable with no VM and no garbage collector. The standard library is statically linked; the only 'runtime' is a thin startup shim and the panic handler.
